today.name: Wizstar R1
today.tagline: Seedance 2.0-level product videos at a lower cost
today.description: Wizstar R1 is an in-house AI video model built for affordable, everyday creation. Combine up to nine reference images and videos to generate 5–15-second videos with native audio, guided by your products, characters, scenes, and styles. R1 excels at animation and 3D content and matches Seedance 2.0's usable-output rate for product videos in internal tests. Eligible members enjoy unlimited, credit-free generation, giving creators more freedom to experiment and refine their ideas.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋I'm part of the marketing team at Wizstar. We're building AI-powered video creation tools to help creators, marketing teams, and businesses produce high-quality video content more efficiently.Creators, marketing teams, and businesses all need to produce videos continuously and at scale. But high generation costs make it expensive to test creative ideas, produce multiple variations, and scale video production.That's why we built Wizstar R1 — a cost-efficient reference-to-video model that balances generation quality and affordability, with generation costs starting at just $0.06 per second.Our goal is to make high-quality AI video generation affordable for people and teams that need to create more, experiment more, and produce at scale.What makes Wizstar R1 different?🖼️ Image + Prompt to Video — Start with a single reference image and a text prompt to generate 5–15-second videos featuring characters, products, and scenes. No source video required.🎯 Consistent Characters & Objects — Preserve subject identity, appearance, and visual details across complex movements and changing scenes, reducing identity drift and unwanted distortions.🎭 Natural Human Performance — Generate natural body movements, expressive facial performances, eye movements, and subtle expressions for more lifelike characters.🔊 Native Audio-Visual Generation — Generate character dialogue, ambient sounds, and rich sound effects together with the video in one generation.💰 Built for High-Volume Creation — At just $0.06 per second, R1 makes it more affordable to explore creative directions, produce multiple variations, and scale video production without constantly worrying about generation costs.Where do we see the biggest potential?We're particularly excited about three areas:Creators: Produce more content, explore different storytelling styles, and keep up with the demand for frequent publishing.Marketing Teams: Generate and test multiple ad creatives, product videos, and campaign variations without stretching production budgets.Businesses: Scale video asset production for e-commerce, product marketing, and other commercial applications.And this is just the beginning.Our vision is to make high-quality AI video generation not only impressive, but also economically viable for everyday production at scale.We'll continue improving reference consistency, motion quality, human expressiveness, and audio-visual generation, while optimizing the balance between quality, speed, and cost.We believe the future of AI video isn't just about generating better videos. It's about making great videos affordable enough to create as many as you need.Try Wizstar R1: https://wizstar.com/models/wizstar-r1We'd love to hear your thoughts: If video generation became significantly more affordable, what would you create more of? 🚀

today.name: Contral
today.tagline: The AI coding agent that checks its work and teaches you
today.description: Contral is out of beta. Use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI or Copilot CLI inside Contral, on your own account. Contral checks every turn against what you asked for and sends smaller models a specific correction, explains every change with a teaching card, and undoes a whole turn in one click. Plus Defense Mode, video explanations by Scrimba, and Learn mode in 5 languages. In VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf and more, or the Contral IDE. Free to start.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! I'm Devansh, co-founder of Contral.Contral is out of beta today: Contral IDE 1.1 and the extension 1.0.The problem we kept hitting: AI agents write code faster than anyone can read it, they say "Done!" when they aren't, and you end up shipping code you can't explain.What's new:Bring your own agent. Use Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI inside Contral, on your own account. Pick the model and effort, approve commands inline, and see every changed file as a diff.Contral checks the agent's work. Free to start: 30 Agent mode messages a day, unlimited on paid and lifetime plans.For the PH community: AppSumo's Black Friday sale takes 10% off our lifetime deal until Dec 1: appsumo.8odi.net/n4JVgxI'd love your feedback, especially on which agent you use and what it gets wrong most often.

today.name: Periscope
today.tagline: Turn any work into an API
today.description: Describe a task and get an endpoint for it. An agent does the work through the screen on its own cloud desktop, in any software, however old. Call it over REST, or from Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor over MCP. The Free plan needs no card.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Rayan, one of the founders of Periscope.I lived in an AI bubble until I started talking to businesses outside tech. Most of them still don't use AI. An agent does the work through the screen on its own cloud desktop. You call it over REST, or ask for it in Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor over MCP. comments.text: Hey Product Hunt,I'm Ravi, co-founder of Scalekit. Today we're launching AgentKit, an MCP gateway that handles auth and tool-calling for AI agents in production.Why now? Over the last year, wiring an agent to a tool got easy. MCP standardized the interface, and any agent can now call Gmail or Salesforce after an afternoon of work.But the tool call is only the surface. Once an agent ships to real users, everything underneath it shows up:whose credentials each call executes withwhich tools each agent should have in contextthe internal systems no catalog coverswhat happens when an upstream API pushes backwho's accountable for every actionThat layer decides whether an agent makes it to production. It's what we built AgentKit for.Try it free: scalekit.com. The free tier includes 10,000 tool calls a month and all 600+ connectors. Make your first tool call from the dashboard, or start from your terminal with npx @ scalekit-inc/cli setup.Here's what it looks like in practice.Say you're shipping a sales agent inside your product. A rep types: "Prep me for the Acme renewal. Pull the deal, the last three email threads, what the team said in Slack, when we last met them, and how much they've used the product this quarter."Four apps, one ask. Getting it working for one rep in a demo is easy. Here's what's underneath when it runs for every rep at every customer:Thousands of OAuth grants, not four. 40 customers × 30 reps × Salesforce, Gmail, Slack and Calendar = 4,800 connected accounts. Each needs its tokens stored, isolated per customer, and refreshed before they expire mid-run. → AgentKit manages connected accounts end to end. Users authorize through an auth link you surface in your app. Tokens live in a per-tenant AES-256 vault, refresh automatically, and are injected at execution time. They never touch your code, logs, or prompts.Every call has to execute as the right user. The agent should see what that rep can see at that customer, and nothing more. Not a shared service account with org-wide access to every inbox. → Every tool call executes with the end user's own credentials, within the scopes they granted.Every tool definition costs context. Gmail alone exposes ~30 tools; four apps put over a hundred on the table. At ~200 tokens per definition, 40 tools burn ~8,000 tokens before the agent does any work, and tool selection gets worse as the list grows. Your prep agent needs about ten tools. Your outbound agent needs a different ten. → Virtual MCP Servers let you compose a tool set per agent role, across connectors. Each role gets one static MCP URL; you mint a short-lived session token per user per run. Smaller context and least-privilege access: ten tool definitions (~2,000 tokens) instead of over a hundred (20,000+).The data you need has no connector. Usage lives in your customer's internal analytics service. No catalog covers it, so you'd build that integration yourself, auth included. → Define it as a custom connector (OAuth 2.0, API key, bearer token, RSA or basic auth), or point AgentKit at a remote MCP server. It runs on the same gateway with the same credential handling and logs as the 600+ built-in connectors.It has to hold up and be auditable. Rate limits, timeouts, upstream errors the model can't act on. Then a deal stage changes and someone asks whether the rep did it or the agent did. → Retries and rate limits are handled on every call. Every call is logged with agent, user, tool and response, and logs stream to Datadog or Splunk.None of this shows up in a demo. All of it shows up in production. AgentKit handles that layer: 30,000+ tools across 600+ apps behind one MCP gateway. And with Triggers, an agent can start on its own the moment an email lands.Python and Node SDKs. Works with the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs, LangChain, Google ADK, Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, and Claude Code. You keep your framework and backend.Which of these five has slowed your agent down the most?

The per-user auth angle is what stood out to me — every action running as the person who asked, inside the scopes they granted, instead of a shared service account. That's the part that usually gets hand-waved until an agent does something it shouldn't. Pairing that with virtual MCP servers that only expose the tools an agent actually needs feels like the right way to keep both permissions and context tight. Curious how the context optimizer decides what to trim when a workflow pulls in a lot of tools.
Curious, out of the 600 apps, which ones do agents actually use the most? Would love to know what people are really automating vs. what is just being demoed and no more than that
Do you sell the app

Congrats Ravi, Satya and team!Curious: for a team that already has an agent running on its own homegrown auth setup, what does switching to AgentKit look like? How long does it take, and what do they get to delete?

Whose credentials, by a mile. We caught a nasty version of it this week before it hit anyone: our scheduled agents ran under the person who approved them, so removing that person from the org would have stopped all their jobs, even though the admin review looked finished. If every call here runs as the user who asked, what happens to scheduled agents and Triggers when that user leaves or loses a scope? Does the agent stop, and who hears about it?

month.aiReview:
مسئله و راه‌حل:
بنیان‌گذاران استارتاپ‌ها وقت زیادی را صرف جلسات بی‌نتیجه با سرمایه‌گذاران می‌کنند و سرمایه‌گذاران نیز با انبوهی از طرح‌های ناآماده روبرو هستند. TheBold با ارزیابی آمادگی استارتاپ از طریق هوش مصنوعی و تایید داده‌های واقعی پیشرفت (Traction)، فقط استارتاپ‌های واجد شرایط را به سرمایه‌گذاران وصل می‌کند.

استفاده از مدل‌های زبانی بزرگ (LLM) برای شبیه‌سازی پرسش و پاسخ‌های دقیق VCها، الگوریتم‌های تطبیق داده‌ها (Matching Engine) بین معیارهای سرمایه‌گذار و وضعیت استارتاپ، و داشبورد تحلیل داده برای ثبت سوابق اجرایی.

مدل درآمدی:
حق اشتراک پریمیوم از بنیان‌گذاران برای ابزارهای تمرینی و شبیه‌ساز، و مدل کارمزدی به ازای معرفی‌های موفق به شبکه سرمایه‌گذاران.

نقاط قوت:

- صرفه‌جویی شدید در زمان سرمایه‌گذاران (Filter کردن طرح‌های ضعیف)
- ایجاد سنجه‌های شفاف برای ارزیابی عملکرد واقعی استارتاپ

نقاط ضعف:
- ابهام در نحوه تعاریف دقیق و راستی‌آزمایی پلتفرم از داده‌های فروش یا مشتریان
- ریسک بالای وابستگی به تمایل سرمایه‌گذاران برای اعتماد به این سیستم واسط

نکته طلایی برای بازار ایران:
در ایران به دلیل فضای سنتی سرمایه‌گذاری، الگوریتم‌های هوش مصنوعی به تنهایی کافی نیستند؛ این محصول باید با VCهای مطرح ایرانی شراکت استراتژیک ببندد تا «گواهی آمادگی هوش مصنوعی» به عنوان یک معیار معتبر ورودی در فرایند غربالگری آن صندوق‌ها پذیرفته شود.

month.name: Creatify Max

month.description: Max is your teammate for paid ads. Share a product URL or brief and Max makes video ads, sets up campaigns on Meta and TikTok, and watches results 24/7, flagging what to fix next. You make the calls: nothing goes live without your approval.

comments.text: Hello, Product Hunters! 👋I’m Yinan, CEO of Creatify. Some of you may remember us from our URL to video ads launch. Thanks to this community, we became the #1 Product of the Day.Today, we’re launching the biggest product we’ve built so far: Creatify Max. Creating an ad is only one part of the job. Paid media teams still spend hours checking dashboards, moving data between tools, repeating campaign setup, and trying to understand why one creative performs better than another.I know this problem firsthand. Before starting Creatify, I built Meta’s first video ad CTR prediction model. Even with great tools, much of the repetitive work remained.That’s why we built Max. It’s an AI teammate that helps across the entire paid advertising workflow.🎬 Create ads: Turn a product URL or creative brief into video ads using Creatify’s own video models.🚀 Launch campaigns: Set up campaigns on Meta and TikTok using your preferred naming conventions, budgets, and targeting.📈 Learn and improve: Monitor performance around the clock, generate reports based on the KPIs you care about, and turn winning ads into briefs for the next creative round. Max remembers your playbook and learns from your feedback, so it becomes more useful over time.🔒 You stay in control: Max never launches anything without your approval. You make the decisions. Max takes care of the repetitive clicks.I’d especially love to hear from marketers and paid media teams:Which part of your advertising workflow would you most want Max to take off your plate?I’ll be here all day to answer questions and hear your feedback.Thanks for stopping by! You can try Max here: https://creatify.ai/ad-agent 🙌

month.aiReview:
مسئله و راه‌حل: ابزار Creatify Max چالش کارهای تکراری و زمان‌بر در مدیریت تبلیغات کلیکی (از ساخت محتوا تا تنظیم کمپین و پایش) را هدف قرار داده است. راه‌حل آن ارائه یک دستیار هوش مصنوعی همه‌جانبه است که فرآیند ساخت ویدیو، راه‌اندازی کمپین در Meta و TikTok و تحلیل شبانه‌روزی را انجام می‌دهد، در حالی که لایه کنترل انسانی (Human-in-the-loop) حفظ شده است.

معماری و تکنولوژی: سیستم از مدل‌های اختصاصی تبدیل URL به ویدیو، الگوریتم‌های پیش‌بینی CTR و خطوط لوله پردازش ویدیو استفاده می‌کند. اتصال از طریق API به بسترهای تبلیغاتی بزرگ و بهره‌گیری از سیستم یادگیری مداوم بر اساس بازخورد کاربر، هسته فنی آن را تشکیل می‌دهد.

مدل درآمدی: مدل SaaS مبتنی بر اشتراک دوره‌ای بر اساس تعداد ویدیوهای تولیدی، کمپین‌های فعال و حجم بودجه تحت مدیریت است.

نقاط قوت:
۱. پوشش کامل چرخه تبلیغات (ایجاد، اجرا، بهینه‌سازی) به‌جای تمرکز صرف بر ساخت محتوا.
۲. حفظ کنترل نهایی توسط کاربر که اعتماد آژانس‌ها را جلب می‌کند.
۳. سابقه بنیان‌گذار در توسعه مدل‌های CTR متا که اعتبار فنی بالایی ایجاد کرده است.

نقاط ضعف:
۱. چالش در مدیریت حالات خاص (Edge Cases) مانند رد شدن تبلیغات یا اختلال در اتریبیوشن.
۲. وابستگی شدید به تغییرات API پلتفرم‌های ثالث (Meta و TikTok).

So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.

year.name: Pazi
year.description: Pazi is an AI team for that idea you keep coming back to — a book, a shop, an app, a skill you want to sell. Tell Pazi what you're trying to do and it builds a team of agents around your idea and starts making things happen: a website, first outreach, content, the next step. Every time you come back, something has moved. You stay in control; your team does the rest alongside you, one real step at a time. Like vibe coding but for business operations.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋I'm Zvonimir, co-founder of Pazi. Some of you might know me from Pythagora / GPT Pilot - one of the first open-source coding agents, 33K GitHub ⭐We built Pythagora thinking people wanted to build software. 100k users later, we realized building was just a means to an end. The moment the app was done, people didn't celebrate. They got stuck. "Now what?"The app was never the point. They didn't want to build applications. They wanted to be entrepreneurs.Every experienced founder knows the hard part comes after the build - getting it in front of people, seeing what lands, changing it, trying again. A business is just that loop, run a few hundred times until something works.So for the last 6 months we've been building Pazi to run that loop with you.You bring an idea. Pazi builds a team of agents around it and starts moving - and it doesn't wait for instructions. It tries something, sees what lands, adjusts, keeps going.Here's one real idea that one of our users started with: a prompt pack to sell on Gumroad.Pazi built her a team - a growth strategist, a content writer, a researcher - and got to work. The pack itself. A cover to drop into Canva, with the hex codes. A posting calendar: which platform, which day, which hook, which call to action. And competitor pricing research she never asked for, because she'd mentioned in passing that she had no idea what to charge.Today, she pays for Pazi and for no other AI tool.We looked at the first 529 ideas people brought us. ~75% of what they actually wanted wasn't "build me an app." It was some version of get me customers. So that's where the agents start.Two years ago, "vibe coding" sounded absurd - many said that only real engineers write real code. The exact same shift is about to hit the way companies run.👉 Soon, no one will run their business operations by hand either. 👈Today is day one. Autonomous companies are rough in some places, just like early vibe coding was too.And if you're someone with an idea and no team: this is the best moment in history to be you. That gap used to kill things before they started. It's about to stop mattering.What would help us most: take an idea you've been sitting on, run it through Pazi for real, and tell us where it broke, what surprised you, and what was missing. My co-founder Leon and the team are here all day, reading every comment.Come build with us 🥂
